source_spans.locator: Institutional abstract: categorization strategies and standard models are evaluated at successive learning stages for smaller less-differentiated and larger more-differentiated category structures.
Institutional abstract: for smaller less-differentiated categories, exemplar-based processing dominates even early in learning.
Institutional abstract: for larger more-differentiated categories, prototype-based processing has a strong early advantage that diminishes slowly.
Institutional abstract: model behavior suggests a psychological transition from prototype-based to exemplar-based processing and different category structures produce different learning trajectories.

Smith & Minda (1998), original article pp. 1416, 1418 and 1425 (Experiments 1, 2 and 4): early prototype-model fit advantage in large, better-differentiated categories depends on experiment/category condition; model fit is not direct identification of participants' internal processing.

Smith & Minda (1998), original article pp. 1422-1423, Figure 6 (Experiment 3), and pp. 1425-1426 (Experiment 4): for small, poorly differentiated categories, exemplar model fits better from early epochs and prototype model has no early fit advantage.

Smith & Minda (1998), original article pp. 1426-1428 (mixture-model interpretation, Figure 9) and p. 1432 (General Discussion): inferred prototype-to-exemplar transition applies particularly to large, better-differentiated categories and does not directly establish a unique cognitive mechanism.

provenance.venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition

conditions: successive stages of category learning under different category structures

temporal_scope: early through later stages of learning

relative fit of the standard exemplar model to observed category-learning performance profiles; a model-comparison result rather than directly measured processing
relative fit of the basic prototype model to observed category-learning performance profiles; a model-comparison result rather than directly measured processing

relations.description: for small, poorly differentiated categories the standard exemplar model describes observed performance better, including at early learning stages; this is a model-fit result, not direct observation of exemplar processing

for large, better-differentiated categories the prototype model has an early fit advantage in the reported qualifying task conditions, but not uniformly across all experimental conditions; this is a model-fit result, not direct observation of prototype processing

the authors interpret the learning-stage model-fit trajectory for large, better-differentiated categories as consistent with a gradual shift from prototype-based toward exemplar-based processing; this is an inferred mechanism, not a uniquely established psychological transition and does not generalize to small, poorly differentiated categories
different category structures produce different trajectories through the space of categorization strategies
